memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob looked up and there was Esau, coming with his four hundred men; so he divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two female servants. He put the female servants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph in the rear. He himself went on ahead and bowed down to the ground seven times as he approached his brother." - Gen 33:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The dreaded moment arrives. Jacob looks up and sees Esau approaching with his four hundred men. His heart must have pounded. He arranges his family with care — and then does something striking: he himself goes out ahead of everyone and bows to the ground seven times as he approaches his brother.

Think of how far Jacob has come. This is the man who once cheated Esau out of the blessing, the man who was told his older brother would serve him. Now he goes first, placing himself in front to face the danger, and bows low again and again in humility before the brother he wronged. The proud supplanter has become a humble servant.

There is courage and humility woven together here. Jacob does not hide behind his family; he steps forward to meet what he fears. And he comes not with defiance but with a bowed head, ready to honour the one he had hurt.

This is often what reconciliation requires of us — the courage to face the person we dread, and the humility to lower ourselves before them. Pride would rather avoid the meeting or approach with excuses. But the path to peace runs through humble courage. Following Christ, who humbled Himself for us, we too can bow low to seek peace with those we have wronged.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a difficult meeting I am avoiding out of fear?
2. Can I approach a wronged person with humility rather than excuses?
3. Where do I need both courage and humility to seek peace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to face the meetings I dread and humility to bow before those I have wronged. Lead me down the path of peace, as You have led me. Amen.
